examples.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.

words.tip: Two third tones in a row: the first one rises, so it sounds like ní hǎo. Between friends people often skip it entirely.
Literally 'again see'. 明天见 (see you tomorrow) reuses 见, a nice pattern to show.

characters.meaning: thank (讠 speech + 射 shè for the sound)
the same character, doubled and said with no tone

words.tip: The second 谢 is toneless. Teach the reply too: 不客气 (bú kèqi, you're welcome).
Goes at the start of a request: 请坐, 请进 (please come in). Also 'to treat': 我请你 = my treat.
Roughly 'can't face you', a real apology. For a light 'excuse me' (getting attention, squeezing past), use 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi).
Same form for I and me. Add 的 for 'my' (我的). Pronouns never change form in Chinese, a relief after German.
The left side 亻 is the 'person' radical. Polite 'you' is 您 (nín), a bit like German Sie.
Sounds exactly like 她 (she). Only the written radical differs: 亻 person.
Same sound as 他 (he). The 女 radical means 'woman'. In speech you can't tell them apart either.
们 makes any pronoun plural: 我们, 你们, 他们. 咱们 (zánmen) means 'we, including you', common in the north.
Links nouns (我是德国人) but not adjectives: say 我很累, never 我是累. It never changes form.
Always negated with 没, never 不: 没有. Also means 'there is': 这里有咖啡 (there's coffee here).
Do and make, like German machen. 做饭 = to cook. Watch out for 作, which has the same sound.
No 'to' needed: 去 + place (去中国, 去超市). 吧 at the end turns it into 'let's'.
Movement towards the speaker, the opposite of 去.

characters.meaning: word ending, no meaning of its own (also in 怎么)

words.tip: Question words sit where the answer would go: 这是什么? = 'this is what?'. No word-order change, unlike German and English.
Two pronunciations: shéi (common in speech) and shuí. Both are correct.
Only the tone separates 哪里 (where) from 那里 (nàlǐ, there). Northern speakers say 哪儿 (nǎr). Also a modest reply to a compliment: 哪里哪里!
Literally 'what time'. It goes before the verb: 你什么时候来?

characters.meaning: word ending, no meaning of its own (also in 什么)

examples.english: How do you read this character?

words.tip: Useful extras: 怎么了? = what's wrong? 怎么样? = how is it? / how about it?
Chinese has no all-purpose 'yes'. You repeat the verb (你去吗? 去!) or say 对 (that's right).
Becomes bú before a 4th tone: 不是 (bú shì), 不要 (bú yào). Used for habits, preferences and the future.
Negates 有 and completed actions: 我没去 (I didn't go). The 不 vs 没 contrast is worth a few examples.
Always before the verb, never at the end of the sentence like English 'too'.
Often just links a subject and an adjective with little 'very' meaning: 我很好 = I'm good. Stress it to mean 'really'.
Show the family: 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 昨天 (zuótiān) yesterday.
明 = sun 日 + moon 月, 'bright'. The same pattern gives 明年 = next year.
Time words go near the start, before the verb: 我现在很忙.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài Běijīng zhù le sān tiān.
examples.english: We stayed in Beijing for three days.

words.tip: Also 'sky' and 'heaven'. Counts on its own with no measure word: 三天 = three days.
Counts on its own like 天: 两年. Chinese New Year (春节, Chūnjié) is a great thing to talk about together.
你吃饭了吗? is a classic friendly greeting, not an invitation. The 口 (mouth) radical shows up in lots of mouth words.

examples.english: What would you like to drink?

words.tip: Another 口 radical. Common pairs: 喝水, 喝茶, 喝酒 (drink alcohol).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi shuǐ.
examples.english: Please give me a glass of water.

words.tip: Many Chinese people drink 热水 (hot water) by default, a good talking point next to German Kohlensäure.
Means both rice and 'a meal': 早饭 breakfast, 午饭 lunch, 晚饭 dinner. 米饭 is specifically rice.
German Tee and English 'tea' come from a southern Chinese pronunciation (tê), 'chai' from chá. Black tea is 红茶, 'red tea'.
Means both home and family. The character is a roof 宀 over a pig 豕, a memorable picture.
间 is also the measure word for rooms. 卧室 (wòshì) = bedroom.
The character looks like a doorway. 开门 / 关门 = open / close the door, and also a shop opening or closing. 个 is fine in casual speech.
住在 + place: 我住在… Like German wohnen, it's about where you live, not being alive (活).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào shàng chuáng shuìjiào le.

words.tip: 张 is the measure word for flat things: beds, tables, paper. 起床 = get up.

characters.meaning: mum (女 woman + 马 mǎ for the sound)
the same character, doubled and said with no tone

examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma zuò de fàn hěn hǎochī.

words.tip: The second syllable is toneless. 母亲 (mǔqīn) is the formal word. Note the 女 radical again.

characters.meaning: dad (父 father + 巴 bā for the sound)
the same character, doubled and said with no tone

words.tip: Same pattern as 妈妈. 父亲 (fùqīn) is formal.
Use 两 (not 二) for 'two' before a measure word: 两个孩子.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.

words.tip: 男朋友 = boyfriend, 女朋友 = girlfriend, the same idea as German Freund / Freundin.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiārén dōu zài Déguó.
examples.english: My family are all in Germany.

words.tip: 家 (from the home session) + 人 person. A good moment to show how words are built from characters already known.

examples.english: I want a cup of coffee.

words.tip: Direct 'want', also 'going to': 我要走了 = I'm off now. 不要 = don't (want).

examples.english: I'd like to go to China.

words.tip: Softer than 要, like German möchte. Also 'think' and 'miss': 我想你 = I miss you.
喜欢 + verb = like doing, the job German gern does. Works for people too: 我喜欢你.
Literally 'high mood'. 很高兴认识你 = nice to meet you, a callback to session 1.
累死了 = exhausted (lit. tired to death), the same exaggeration as German todmüde.
女 woman + 子 child = good, a classic picture. 好 + verb means 'nice to': 好吃 (tasty), 好看 (good-looking).
A person with arms stretched wide. Also age: 你多大? = how old are you (to peers and adults).
Also a friendly nickname prefix: 小王 = 'little Wang'. 太…了 = too…

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de xīn shǒujī.

words.tip: Already seen in 新年快乐. Goes straight before short nouns without 的: 新书, 新车.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de lǎo péngyou.
examples.english: He's an old friend of mine.

words.tip: For people and relationships (老朋友, 老师). Old things use 旧 (jiù): 旧手机. As a prefix it's affectionate: 老王.
The tone shifts: yí before a 4th tone (一个 yí ge), yì before the others (一天 yì tiān), yī when counting or alone.
For counting and in numbers (二十 = 20, 二月 = February). Before a measure word use 两 instead: 两个人.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
examples.english: There are three people in my family.

words.tip: One, two, three are just one, two, three strokes. 口 (mouth) is the measure word for family members.
Sounds like 死 (sǐ, death), so 4 is unlucky and some buildings skip the 4th floor. Tongue twister: 四是四，十是十.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǔ ge rén qù chīfàn.
examples.english: The five of us are going to eat.

words.tip: Show the one-handed Chinese counting gestures for 1–10. They're different from German finger counting.
Before a measure word many people say zhèi: 这个 zhège / zhèige. Both are fine.
那 (nà, that) and 哪 (nǎ, which) differ by tone, and 哪 has the 口 radical that marks many question words.
Northern speakers say 这儿 (zhèr). Same pattern as 哪里 from session 4.
Northern: 那儿 (nàr). Only the tone separates it from 哪里 (nǎlǐ, where), so drill the pair.

examples.english: The book is on the table.

words.tip: Says where something is: 我在这里. Before a verb it means 'in the middle of': 我在吃饭 = I'm eating.

examples.english: You and I will go together.

words.tip: Only joins nouns (我和你), never two sentences, unlike German und. Many speakers say 跟 (gēn) instead.

examples.english: Do you drink tea or coffee?

words.tip: 'Or' in questions. In statements use 或者 (huòzhě): 茶或者咖啡都可以 = tea or coffee are both fine.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lèi, dànshì hěn gāoxìng.

words.tip: Often shortened to 但. 可是 (kěshì) is a softer spoken alternative.

examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒmen zài jiā.
examples.english: Because it's raining, we're staying home.

words.tip: The 'because' part normally comes first, whereas German usually puts the weil part second. Often paired with 所以.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lèi, suǒyǐ zǎo diǎn shuì.
examples.english: I'm tired, so I'll go to bed early.

words.tip: Chinese happily says 因为… 所以… in one sentence ('because…, so…'), which sounds doubled up in English and German.

examples.english: How do you say it in Chinese?

words.tip: 用中文怎么说? is the most useful sentence for these sessions. 讠 is the 'speech' radical.

words.gloss: to look, to watch, to read
words.tip: A hand 手 over an eye 目, shading your eyes to look. Also read (看书) and visit (看朋友).
听说… = I heard that… 听懂 = to understand by listening.
Knowing facts, like German wissen. In speech 道 is often toneless: zhīdao.
Knowing people, like German kennen. Also recognising characters: 你认识这个字吗?

examples.english: I can speak a little Chinese.

words.tip: For learned skills (languages, swimming), and 'will probably': 明天会下雨 = it'll probably rain tomorrow.
Ability or circumstances allowing. 会 (know how), 能 (able) and 可以 (allowed) make a great trio to explain.
Permission, like German dürfen. 可以! on its own = sure, OK. Two 3rd tones: sounds like kéyǐ.

examples.english: You should go to bed earlier.

words.tip: Advice or expectation, like German sollen. Also 'probably': 他应该到了 = he should be there by now.
Strong necessity. 'Don't have to' is 不用 (bú yòng), not 不必须, the same trap as German muss nicht.

examples.pinyin: Shànghǎi shì yí ge dà chéngshì.

words.tip: A walled market: 城 (wall) + 市 (market). Talk about which cities each of you has lived in.
条 is the measure word for long thin things: roads, rivers, fish. 一路平安 = have a safe trip.

examples.pinyin: Tā de chē shì xīn de.

words.tip: Any vehicle: 汽车 (car), 火车 (train, 'fire vehicle'), 自行车 (bicycle). Driving yourself is 开车.
Sitting, and riding as a passenger: 坐车, 坐飞机. Two people 人人 on the ground 土. Same sound as 做 (do).
Literally 'vehicle stand'. 火车站 = train station, 地铁站 = metro station.
Both a noun and a verb. The place comes before the verb: 在 + place + 工作.
Learning plus practising. 学 alone works too: 学中文.
大学 (dàxué) = university, 'big learning'. 个 works as the measure word in speech.
看书 = to read. 书店 = bookshop.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de Zhōngwén lǎoshī.

words.tip: Also how you address a teacher: 王老师. Fitting, since you're each other's 老师 now.

examples.pinyin: Xià ge xīngqī wǒmen qù Běijīng.
examples.english: Next week we're going to Beijing.

words.tip: Days are numbered: 星期一 is Monday through 星期六 Saturday. Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日.
早! on its own is a casual 'morning!'. 早饭 = breakfast.
Covers evening and night. 晚安 (wǎn'ān) = good night, said at bedtime like Gute Nacht.
几点? = what time is it? 三点半 = 3:30, so no German-style 'half to four'. 一点儿 = a little.
Time as an amount, like German Zeit. Clock time uses 点. 没有时间 = no time.
买 (mǎi, buy) and 卖 (mài, sell) differ only by tone and the 十 on top. Drill them as a pair.
Falling tone, the partner of 买. 买卖 (mǎimai, 'buy-sell') = business.
The 钅 radical means metal, because early money was metal. Prices use 块 (kuài) in speech, 元 (yuán) in writing.
Literally 'many-few'. 多少钱? is the shopping question. For small numbers people use 几 (jǐ) instead.
太贵了! is essential at markets. Also 'honourable': 您贵姓? = may I ask your surname?
A lucky number: 六 sounds like 流 (flowing smoothly), so 666 means 'awesome' online.

examples.pinyin: Yí ge xīngqī yǒu qī tiān.

words.tip: Note the q, which sounds like 'ch' in 'cheese'. A good one for practising pinyin spelling.
The luckiest number: 八 sounds like 发 (fā, to prosper). The Beijing Olympics opened at 8:08 pm on 8/8/2008.
Sounds like 久 (jiǔ, long-lasting), so it's popular around weddings.
Bigger numbers are perfectly regular: 十一 = 11, 二十 = 20, 九十九 = 99. Compare German neunundneunzig, which says the ones first.

examples.english: There are lots of people here.

words.tip: A person walking on two legs. Nationalities add 人: 德国人 (German), 中国人 (Chinese).
男 is a field 田 over strength 力: the one working the field. 男朋友 = boyfriend.
Note the ü in nǚ. The 女 radical has turned up in 她, 妈妈 and 好.

examples.english: The girl is reading a book.

words.tip: Also 女孩子. Boy = 男孩. Fun contrast: German das Mädchen is grammatically neuter.
Surnames come first: 王小明 = Wang Xiaoming. Talk about what each of your names means.
Turns anything into 'X's': 我的 (my), 妈妈的 (mum's). Often dropped for close family and friends: 我妈妈.
Like German ihr (you all). Same 们 as 我们 from session 2.
她们 for an all-female group; mixed groups use 他们. All sound the same.
Adds 'myself / yourself': 你自己去吧 = go by yourself. 自己的 = one's own.
Literally 'big family'. Matches German alle. 大家好 opens almost every speech.
A verb-plus-object pair that can be split: 睡了一个好觉 = had a good sleep. 觉 is read jué in 觉得 (session 26).
Reading aloud, or studying (读大学 = go to university). Reading for fun is often just 看书.

examples.english: How do you write this character?

words.tip: 这个字怎么写? will be your most-asked question. Practise stroke order together.

examples.english: The kids are playing in the park.

words.tip: Also 'hang out': 周末去哪儿玩? Sports and instruments use other verbs (打篮球, 弹钢琴), unlike German spielen.
等一下 = wait a moment. At the end of a list it means 'etc.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū.

words.tip: Also 'for / to': 给你打电话 = call you. 给你! = here you go.
There's a hand 手 at the bottom. 拿走 = take away, 拿来 = bring over.

examples.english: Don't forget to bring your keys.

words.tip: Taking something or someone with you. 带孩子 = to look after the kids.
帮忙 (bāngmáng) is the 'help out' form: 谢谢你帮忙. 帮我 + verb = do something for me.
Stronger than 要. 不需要 = no need.
Opinions and feelings, like German glauben or finden. 我觉得很好 = I think it's good.

examples.text: 我可以问你一个问题吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí ma?
examples.english: Can I ask you a question?

words.tip: A mouth 口 inside a door 门: asking at the door. 问题 = question; 没问题 = no problem.
告诉 + person + thing. 我告诉你 = let me tell you.
听懂 = understand by listening, 看懂 = understand by reading. 我不懂 = I don't get it.
A learner's best friend: …是什么意思? Also 有意思 = interesting, 不好意思 = excuse me.
Literally 'sky air'. 天气预报 = weather forecast.
阳 is the 'yang' of yin and yang. The older word 日 lives on in 日本 (Japan, 'sun's origin').
Rain 'falls down': 下雨, and snow is 下雪. No 'it' needed, unlike German es regnet.
The four dots at the bottom (灬) mean fire. 热水 (hot water) came up in session 7.
The two strokes on the left (冫) mean ice. 我很冷 = I'm cold, simpler than German Mir ist kalt.
The colour of luck: red envelopes (红包) at New Year. Add 色 for the colour as a noun: 红色.
The grass radical 艹 on top: blue dye originally came from a plant.
Another ü: lǜ. 绿茶 (green tea) from session 7.
Fire 灬 at the bottom: soot. 天黑了 = it's got dark.
Also 'for nothing': 白跑一趟 = a wasted trip. 明白 (clear and bright) = to understand.
Goes before the verb like other adverbs. 一直 (yìzhí) means 'all along, continuously'.
Doubled for emphasis. 经常 (jīngcháng) means the same.
For past experiences use 从来没…过: 我从来没去过德国 = I've never been to Germany.
Usually paired with 了 at the end: 已经…了.
Still, also, and 还没 = not yet: 我还没吃. The same character as in 还是 (session 14).
…疼 = …hurts: 头疼, 肚子疼 (stomach ache). 头 is also the measure word for cattle.
手机 = mobile phone ('hand machine'), just like German Handy.
A pair of eyes: 一双眼睛. The 目 radical (an eye) also appears in 看.
The 疒 radical means illness (also in 疼). 多喝热水 (drink lots of hot water) is the classic advice!

examples.english: I need to see a doctor.

words.tip: 看医生 = to see a doctor. 医院 = hospital.
件 counts tops and single garments. 衣 shrinks to 衤 on the left of clothing characters, as in 裤.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài cháng le.

words.tip: One pair of trousers is 一条裤子, not 一双: 条 is for long, thin things. 短裤 (duǎnkù) = shorts.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi yì shuāng xié.
examples.english: I want to buy a pair of shoes.

words.tip: 一双鞋 = a pair of shoes, 一只鞋 = one shoe. Many homes have slippers (拖鞋) waiting at the door: 换鞋 = change your shoes.

words.gloss: to wear, to put on (clothes, shoes)

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān hěn lěng, duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
examples.english: It's cold today, wear something warm.

words.tip: 穿 is for things you get into: clothes, trousers, shoes, socks. Hats, glasses and watches take 戴 instead, where German uses tragen for both.
Contrast with 穿: 戴帽子 (hat), 戴眼镜 (glasses), 戴手表 (watch). Don't mix it up with 带 (to bring), which sounds exactly the same.

examples.english: Mum is cooking in the kitchen.

words.tip: Same 房 as 房间. 厨师 (chúshī) = chef.
Literally 'make a meal'. It's verb + object, so it can split: 做了饭, 做中国饭. Ask who does the cooking in each of your families.

examples.english: The book is on the table.

words.tip: 张 counts flat surfaces: tables, beds, paper, photos. 桌 has 木 (wood) at the bottom.

characters.meaning: plate, tray (皿 dish at the bottom)

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí ge pánzi.
examples.english: Could you pass me a plate?

words.tip: 皿 at the bottom is a picture of a dish. 盘 also works as a measure for food: 一盘饺子 = a plate of dumplings.
杯 is also the measure for drinks: 一杯茶 (a cup of tea) vs 一个杯子 (a cup). 干杯 (gānbēi) = cheers!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān chī yí ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: I eat an apple every day.

words.tip: Also the brand: 苹果手机 = iPhone. On Christmas Eve (平安夜) people give apples, because 苹 sounds like 平 in 平安 (peace, safety).
Literally 'water fruit'. 种 = kind: 三种水果 = three kinds of fruit. A plate of cut-up fruit after dinner is a classic way Chinese families show care.

examples.pinyin: Duō chī shūcài duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Eating lots of vegetables is good for you.

words.tip: Both characters have the grass radical 艹. In everyday speech people often just say 菜, as in 买菜 (to buy groceries).
Plain 肉 often means pork; 牛肉 = beef, 鸡肉 = chicken. At the market meat is sold by the 斤 (half a kilo).

examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang wǒ chī le liǎng ge jīdàn.
examples.english: I had two eggs this morning.

words.tip: Literally 'chicken egg'. 西红柿炒鸡蛋 (tomato and egg stir-fry) is the classic first dish to cook together.

examples.english: The food at this restaurant is great.

words.tip: 家 counts businesses. 馆 is a building for a purpose, as in 咖啡馆 (café) and 图书馆 (library).
Show how to call the staff: 服务员，点菜! Dishes usually go in the middle for everyone to share, so ordering is a group decision.
Two meanings: vegetables (买菜) and a dish of food (中国菜 = Chinese food). 道 counts the dishes in a meal: 一道菜.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò de fàn hěn hǎochī!

words.tip: 好 + verb = nice to …: 好喝 (nice to drink), 好看 (nice to look at), 好听 (nice to hear). The opposite is 不好吃 or 难吃.
Calling out 服务员! across the room is normal, not rude. 员 marks someone's job, as in 售货员 (shop assistant).

examples.english: We're travelling to Germany in the summer.

words.tip: Note the ü: lǚ. 旅游 (lǚyóu) is the everyday word for a sightseeing trip.
Literally 'flying machine'. You 坐 (sit on) any transport: 坐飞机, 坐车. 架 counts planes: 一架飞机.

examples.english: I'll pick you up at the airport.

words.tip: 机 here is short for 飞机. Useful pair: 接 = pick someone up, 送 = see someone off.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de xíngli tài duō le!

words.tip: Uncountable like German Gepäck, so count pieces: 两件行李. 行 is xíng here, not háng (as in 银行, bank), and 李 is also the surname Li.
It's a booklet, so it takes 本 like a book. 照 is also in 照片 (photo).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.english: My home is close to the school.

words.tip: Pattern: A 离 B 很近 = A is close to B. The 辶 radical (walking) shows up in lots of movement and distance words.

examples.english: Is the airport far from here?

words.tip: The opposite of 近, with the same 辶 radical. Watch the tone: yuǎn (far) vs yuán (as in 元, the currency).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī zài zhuōzi shang.

words.tip: It comes after the noun: 桌子上 = on the table. Also 'up' and 'previous': 上楼 (go upstairs), 上个星期 (last week).

examples.english: The cat is under the bed.

words.tip: The mirror of 上, also after the noun: 床下, 桌子下面. Also 'next': 下个星期 = next week. Both characters are a stroke above or below a line.

examples.english: The station is right next to the school.

words.tip: Pattern: A 在 B 旁边 = A is next to B. Point at things around the room and practise: 我在你旁边.

examples.english: What time are we meeting tomorrow?

words.tip: Literally 'see face'. It takes no object: say 跟他见面 (meet him), never 见面他. Tell each other about the first time you met.
我到了 is the message you send when you arrive. Also 'to' with places and times: 从八点到十点 = from eight to ten.
回家 = go home. 回来 = come back, 回去 = go back. The character is a box inside a box, like something coming round again.

examples.text: 今天晚上我们出去吃饭吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang wǒmen chūqù chīfàn ba.

words.tip: 出 + 去/来 shows direction: 出去 = go out (away from the speaker), 出来 = come out (towards the speaker). The 去 is often said lightly, chūqu.
请进 is what you say when someone knocks. 进 (enter) and 近 (near) sound exactly the same, so compare the characters.
No past tense needed: the time word does the work. Complete the set: 前天 (day before yesterday), 昨天, 今天, 明天.

examples.english: What do you want to do at the weekend?

words.tip: 周 is another word for week, like 星期. 末 is a tree 木 with a stroke marking the tip: the end. 周末快乐 = have a nice weekend.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān qǐ de hěn zǎo.

words.tip: 早! on its own means 'morning!' (short for 早上好). The sun 日 just coming up over the horizon.

examples.pinyin: Tài wǎn le, wǒmen huí jiā ba.

words.tip: Also 'evening', as in 晚上 and 晚安 (good night). 我来晚了 = sorry I'm late.

examples.english: I have to work on Monday.

words.tip: The days are just numbered: 星期一 to 星期六, but Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日. 一 keeps its first tone here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xià ge yuè qù Zhōngguó.
examples.english: We're going to China next month.

words.tip: 三月 = March, but 三个月 = three months: the 个 makes all the difference. The moon itself is usually 月亮 (yuèliang).

examples.english: Let's go to the seaside in summer.

words.tip: Every season is just season + 天. 夏 (summer) is fourth tone, the same sound as 下.
冬 (winter) sounds like 东 (east). Tell them apart by the two dots at the bottom of 冬, like the ice in 冷.
春节 (Spring Festival) is Chinese New Year, which marks the start of spring in the lunar calendar. Note the sun 日 at the bottom of 春.
秋 is grain 禾 next to fire 火: harvest time. At the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节) families eat mooncakes (月饼).
Literally 'hard to get through'. The everyday word for feeling down; 伤心 (shāngxīn) is stronger, heartbroken.
Takes its object directly: 我怕黑 = I'm afraid of the dark. 忄 on the left is the heart radical, found in many feeling words.
Many people rarely say 我爱你 out loud and show it in actions instead. 520 (wǔ èr líng) sounds like 我爱你, so 20 May is a romantic day.
笑 covers both laughing and smiling; 微笑 (wēixiào) is specifically a smile. Online, 哈哈哈 = haha.
Two mouths 口 over a dog 犬: a howl. Watch the tone: kū (cry) vs kǔ (苦, bitter).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī méi diàn le.

words.tip: 'Hand machine', just like German Handy. Practise asking for a number: 你的手机号是多少?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wǎnshang gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.

words.tip: Pattern: 给 + person + 打电话 = call someone. 打 is a do-everything verb: 打球 (play ball), 打车 (take a taxi).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàndào wǒ de xiāoxi le ma?

words.tip: 发消息 = send a message, e.g. on WeChat (微信). 好消息 = good news. 条 counts messages and news items.

examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ kànkan nǐ de zhàopiàn.

words.tip: 张, because a photo is flat. 拍照 = take a photo. Many speakers say zhàopiān in everyday speech.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo tài lǎo le.

words.tip: Literally 'electric brain'. 台 counts machines and appliances: 一台电脑. A laptop is 笔记本 (notebook).
Also 'likely to': 冬天容易生病 = it's easy to get sick in winter. The opposite is 难.

examples.english: Chinese characters are hard to write.

words.tip: 难 + verb = hard to …, or unpleasant to …: 难吃 (tastes bad), 难看 (ugly). The same 难 as in 难过 (sad).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de tài kuài le!

words.tip: Also 'soon': 快…了 = about to, as in 快到了 (almost there). It has the heart radical 忄, as in 快乐 (happy).

examples.english: Please speak a bit more slowly.

words.tip: The learner's lifeline: 请说慢一点. 慢慢来 = take your time. Same heart radical 忄 as 快.
The opposite of 对. 不错 (búcuò, 'not wrong') means 'pretty good' and is a very common compliment.
Can be followed by another verb: 开始学中文 = start learning Chinese. Also a noun: 一开始 = at first.

examples.english: What time does the film finish?

words.tip: For events ending: films, classes, meetings. To say you've finished doing something, use verb + 完: 我吃完了 = I've finished eating.
Goes before the verb, and pairs with 然后 or 再: 先吃饭，然后看电影. 先生 (xiānsheng) = Mr; husband.

examples.english: Wash your hands first, then eat.

words.tip: Great for telling stories: …然后…然后…. Don't confuse it with 以后 (yǐhòu), 'later, in the future'.

examples.english: In the end we went to Beijing.

words.tip: Also 'last': 最后一天 = the last day. 最 + adjective = most: 最好, 最大.
扇 (shàn) counts windows and doors: 一扇门. Many Chinese families air rooms every day, much like German Lüften.
把 counts things you can grab by a handle: chairs, keys, knives, umbrellas (一把伞). 椅 has 木 (wood) on the left, like 桌.
钥 is read yào here. 钅 on the left is the metal radical. 把 counts keys: 一把钥匙.
开灯 / 关灯 = turn the light on / off. 火 on the left: lamps used to be flames. 盏 (zhǎn) is the classic measure, 个 is fine in speech.

characters.meaning: to send out (used for its sound)

examples.pinyin: Tā zài shāfā shang shuìzháo le.
examples.english: He fell asleep on the sofa.

words.tip: A sound loan from 'sofa': the characters just spell the sound. Find others together: 咖啡 (coffee), 巧克力 (chocolate).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yǎng yì zhī gǒu.
examples.english: I'd like to get a dog.

words.tip: 养 (yǎng) = to keep a pet. 犭 is the animal radical, also in 猫. 一条狗 is common too, especially in the north.
The sound part 苗 (miáo) echoes the meow, and cats say 喵 (miāo). Same animal radical 犭 as 狗.

examples.pinyin: Ménkǒu yǒu yì kē dà shù.
examples.english: There's a big tree by the door.

words.tip: 棵 (kē) counts trees and plants. 木 on the left means wood: 木 alone is a tree, 林 a wood, 森林 a forest.
Literally 'moving thing'. 动物园 = zoo. Ask each other's zodiac animal: 你属什么?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù pá shān ba.
examples.english: Let's go hiking at the weekend.

words.tip: A picture of three peaks. 爬山 ('climb mountain') means hiking. 座 counts big, solid things: mountains, bridges, buildings.
乐 has two readings: yuè (music) and lè (happy, as in 快乐). Swap favourite songs from each country.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān yùndòng bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I exercise for half an hour every day.

words.tip: Also a noun: 你喜欢什么运动? = what sports do you like? The same 动 (move) as in 动物.
Verb + object like 做饭: 唱一首歌 = sing a song. 去唱歌 usually means going to KTV (karaoke), a very popular night out.
Literally 'jump a dance'. Talk about 广场舞: groups dancing together in squares and parks every evening, often retirees.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
examples.english: Let's go to the cinema tonight.

words.tip: 'Electric shadows'. 看电影 = watch a film, 电影院 = cinema. 部 counts films, just like phones.

examples.text: 我可以问你一个问题吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí ma?
examples.english: Can I ask you a question?

words.tip: Both 'question' and 'problem': 没问题 = no problem! 问 is a mouth 口 in a doorway 门.
Literally 'return an answer', with the same 回 as 回家. 答 has bamboo ⺮ on top.
Two third tones in a row, so it's said yéxǔ. 可能 (kěnéng) means the same and is just as common.
当然 works as a full answer on its own: 你爱我吗？当然! The same 然 as in 然后.
Also 'must be': 你一定很累 = you must be tired. 不一定 = not necessarily. 一 becomes yí before the fourth tone of 定.
便 is usually biàn (as in 方便, convenient) but pián here. The bargaining line: 能便宜一点吗? = can you make it cheaper?

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn jǐ diǎn guānmén?
examples.english: What time does this shop close?

words.tip: 家 counts businesses. 店 on its own turns up everywhere: 书店 (bookshop), 饭店 (restaurant, hotel).
Arguing over who pays the bill is a classic ritual, and insisting 我来! is polite. Most people pay by phone with WeChat Pay or Alipay.

examples.text: 我在一家德国公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yì jiā Déguó gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: I work for a German company.

words.tip: 家 counts companies, like 饭馆 and 商店. 去公司 is how people often say 'go to the office'.

examples.english: I'm going to buy a few things.

words.tip: Literally 'east-west'. Keep xi toneless: with a full tone, dōngxī means 'east and west'. 买东西 = go shopping.
It takes no object: say 跟她结婚 (marry her), never 结婚她. 结 is the knot from 结束, and 婚 has the 女 radical.

examples.english: Our wedding is in the summer.

words.tip: 场 (chǎng) counts events: 一场婚礼. Red is the wedding colour, and guests give money in red envelopes (红包).
Goes before the verb, often with 和 or 跟: 我和你一起去. 一 becomes yì before the third tone of 起.

examples.english: You have such a kind heart.

words.tip: Also 'mind'. The heart radical 忄 in 快, 慢 and 怕 is a squeezed 心. 小心 ('small heart') = be careful!
In everyday speech plain 想 works too: 我想你 = I miss you. Both 想 and 念 have 心 (heart) at the bottom.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ hào?

words.tip: Dates go from big to small: 五月二十号 = 20 May. Long-life noodles (长寿面) are the traditional birthday dish.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gěi nǐ de lǐwù.
examples.english: This is a present for you.

words.tip: Never give a clock (送钟 sounds like 'attending a funeral') or share a pear (分梨 sounds like 'separate'). Gifts are often politely refused once before being accepted.

examples.text: 我们怎么庆祝你的生日？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zěnme qìngzhù nǐ de shēngrì?
examples.english: How shall we celebrate your birthday?

words.tip: Works for big and small occasions: 庆祝新年. 国庆节 (National Day, 1 October) uses the same 庆.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ jiā yǒu ge jùhuì.
examples.english: We're having a get-together at ours this weekend.

words.tip: More 'get-together' than wild party: friends or classmates meeting up for food and chat. 会 here means 'meeting', not 'can'.
祝你… is how to give any good wish: 祝你好运 (good luck), 祝你一路平安 (safe journey). Sing 祝你生日快乐 to the Happy Birthday tune.
